item.title: Mossad joins investigation into alleged foreign meddling in Israel elections: Report
item.description: Citing an unverified report by Channel 12, the Times of Israel reported the development, adding that authorities suspect interference extending beyond Qatar to include additional foreign nations.
item.content:encoded:
Mossad joins investigation into alleged foreign meddling in Israel elections: Report Citing an unverified report by Channel 12, the Times of Israel reported the development, adding that authorities suspect interference extending beyond Qatar to include additional foreign nations. ANI | Updated: 30-10-2026 22:11 IST | Created: 30-10-2026 22:11 IST

People walk next to a campaign banner of Netanyahu's Likud party in Bnei Brak, Israel (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Israel's Mossad intelligence agency is reportedly assisting the Shin Bet security service in an investigation into alleged foreign meddling in the recent national election. Citing an unverified report by Channel 12, the Times of Israel reported the development, adding that authorities suspect interference extending beyond Qatar to include additional foreign nations. The ongoing inquiry focuses on allegations surrounding efforts to pay Arab voters in an attempt to boost turnout at polling stations. However, the Central Elections Committee has emphasised that the scope of the probe remains limited and does not cast doubt on the overall election results. Earlier on Thursday, Shin Bet (Israel's Security Agency) stated that information regarding alleged voter fraud in the recent election stems entirely from internal intelligence on foreign influence campaigns, rather than “any political party or political actor on either side of the political map." According to The Times of Israel, the agency emphasised that access to the intelligence remained strictly restricted to internal security personnel and Central Elections Committee (CEC) chair Justice Noam Sohlberg until polls closed, The Times of Israel reported. Reaffirming its commitment to statutory boundaries, the Shin Bet stressed that it is operating exclusively under its legal mandate, with all measures being executed by professional staff and internal legal counsel. Addressing allegations surrounding substantial Qatari funding intended to sway Arab turnout—which reached high levels during Tuesday’s vote—the agency clarified that its inquiry is “focused and limited in scope, and does not cast aspersions on or accuse an entire sector that went out to vote democratically and legally.” “Only those who acted in violation of the law will be dealt with,” the agency stated, as reported by The Times of Israel. Additionally, the Shin Bet confirmed that its chief, David Zini, held high-level briefings over the past day with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, and opposition leader Yair Lapid to outline the core suspicions currently under review. The agency noted that these briefings were conducted with the authorisation and at the explicit request of Sohlberg. Addressing ongoing inquiries, the Shin Bet noted that its investigation remains active, cautioning that “any statements concerning the content or nature of the suspicions do not reflect the agency’s position.” Once concluded, the agency stated it will submit its final findings directly to Sohlberg, “who is the authorised decision-maker on this matter.” The statement comes amid heightened political scrutiny following demands for inquiries into alleged voting irregularities and foreign interference surrounding the election. While Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the controversy as an “earthquake”, alleging that foreign entities had interfered in the elections in favour of Arab parties and called on Zionist parties to reject cooperation with Ra’am and the Joint List, Incumbent Minister of National Security and Chairman of Otzma Yehudit, Itamar Ben Gvir, called for the arrest of the Arab party bosses and alleged the involvement of money from Qatar. However, Qatar has strongly denied claims that it interfered in Israel’s elections, accusing "certain Israeli politicians" of exploiting its name to serve domestic political interests and cover up their own failures. In an official statement published on X, Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari rejected allegations of funding activities aimed at influencing the vote, warning that Doha will not stay silent while being dragged into Israel's internal politics. Similarly, Arab political parties in Israel have also rejected allegations linking them to suspected foreign funding and interference in the Tuesday polls. This comes as the Central Elections Committee of Israel published the final results of the national election, confirming the distribution of seats in the 26th Knesset, which is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10. The pro-Netanyahu bloc secured 53 seats, falling short of the majority required to form a government. According to The Times of Israel, the Likud party, led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, followed by Yashar with 21 seats. B’Yachad secured 12 seats, while the Joint List won 11. The Democrats and Ra’am secured eight seats each, while Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit won seven seats each. Shas and Religious Zionism secured six seats apiece. The final results leave the pro-Netanyahu bloc with 53 seats, the anti-Netanyahu bloc with 48 seats and the Arab factions with 19 seats, according to The Times of Israel. The final voter turnout stood at 77.9 per cent of eligible voters, with 5,716,665 votes cast. The Reservists, which secured 2.7 per cent of the vote, People of Israel with 1.7 per cent and Charedi Public with 0.2 per cent failed to cross the 3.25 per cent electoral threshold. The final official results will be submitted to Israeli President Isaac Herzog on November 4, following examinations of possible errors or inquiries. The newly elected Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Tibetan woman stages fresh protest in Lhasa, demands justice for imprisoned brother Dorje Tashi According to Phayul, Gonpo Kyi has been leading a sustained campaign for her brother’s release and judicial review for several years. Her efforts have included solo demonstrations, sit-ins, prayer vigils and hunger strikes outside government offices, police stations and courts in Lhasa. ANI | Updated: 30-10-2026 20:05 IST | Created: 30-10-2026 20:05 IST

Representative image (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Tibetan woman Gonpo Kyi staged another peaceful protest outside the High People’s Court of the so-called Tibet Autonomous Region (TAR) in Lhasa on October 26, demanding justice for her imprisoned brother, Dorje Tashi, according to a report by Phayul. A newly surfaced video circulating on X (formerly Twitter) reportedly shows Gonpo Kyi protesting outside the court, seeking a review of her brother’s life sentence, a retrial and permission to visit him in prison. According to Phayul, Gonpo Kyi has been leading a sustained campaign for her brother’s release and judicial review for several years. Her efforts have included solo demonstrations, sit-ins, prayer vigils and hunger strikes outside government offices, police stations and courts in Lhasa. Dorje Tashi, once a prominent Tibetan businessman, was arrested in the aftermath of the 2008 protests in occupied Tibet. He was reportedly subjected to months of torture while in detention. In 2010, following a closed-door trial at the Lhasa Intermediate People’s Court, he was sentenced to life imprisonment on charges of loan fraud. However, his supporters have maintained that the charges were politically motivated. His brother, Dorje Tseten, was sentenced to six years in prison in the same case and was subsequently released. Phayul reported that Dorje Tashi’s family has repeatedly pursued judicial review through various legal channels since his imprisonment. In 2020, Chinese authorities rejected appeals filed by his lawyer and relatives seeking reconsideration of his conviction. Between 2023 and 2024, Gonpo Kyi, her husband Choekyong and her brother Dorje Tseten reportedly staged more than seven hunger strikes and prayer protests outside government offices and courts in Lhasa, demanding a review of the life sentence and permission for family visits. The report also highlighted alleged repeated physical assaults, police beatings, interrogations and both short- and long-term detentions faced by Gonpo Kyi and her family in connection with their campaign. On August 20, 2025, Gonpo Kyi reportedly jumped from the second floor of the Yak Hotel in Lhasa in an apparent suicide attempt after being denied permission to visit her brother and allegedly placed under hotel arrest. She sustained serious injuries and was left in critical condition. The case has also attracted international attention, with both the United States and the European Union raising concerns over Dorje Tashi’s imprisonment. According to Phayul, during the 51st session of the UN Human Rights Council, held from September 12 to October 7, 2022, the European Union called for the immediate and unconditional release of several individuals, including Dorje Tashi. The US Department of State also documented Dorje Tashi’s detention in its 2021 and 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices on China, highlighting his case in its assessment of human rights conditions in the country. (ANI)

item.title: Iranian Navy says it destroyed "enemy submarine" and damaged two oil tankers near Strait of Hormuz
item.description: "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement said.
item.content:encoded:
Iranian Navy says it destroyed "enemy submarine" and damaged two oil tankers near Strait of Hormuz "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement said. ANI | Updated: 30-10-2026 18:35 IST | Created: 30-10-2026 18:35 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iranian naval forces destroyed an "enemy submarine" and damaged two commercial oil tankers in the operational zone east of the strategic Strait of Hormuz on Friday morning. State media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) reported, citing the Iranian Navy's Public Relations department, that Iranian forces targeted and destroyed an adversary submarine navigating the operational sector near the vital maritime choke point. "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement said. In a separate development, state broadcasters reported that two oil tankers caught fire in the same maritime zone after striking sea mines. Iranian officials attributed the incident to the vessels ignoring official maritime safety warnings and operating covertly. "Two enemy tankers, which, regardless of the warnings and regulations announced, were travelling in prohibited and unsafe areas east of the Strait of Hormuz with their tracking systems turned off, were damaged and caught fire after hitting naval mines," the statement added. Iranian naval authorities explicitly placed the blame for the incident on the commercial operators, asserting through IRIB that vessel owners would be held accountable for navigating unauthorised routes. "The tanker owners will bear full responsibility for the consequences of unauthorised traffic and disregard for safety and maritime warnings," the statement warned. Reiterating a strict security posture over the regional waterways, the Iranian Armed Forces issued a direct warning against any unauthorised presence or military probing near Iranian territorial interests. "We warn the enemy that any movement, infiltration, or provocative action in areas under the supervision of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will be met with a strong and proportionate response," the statement concluded. The incident comes amid heightened tensions over maritime traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian military authorities asserting control over the waterway and warning commercial vessels against transiting through areas they consider restricted and unsafe. Iran's Army Navy Public Relations, in a statement reported by state broadcaster IRIB, claimed that a tanker travelling in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz had caught fire after striking a naval mine."This morning, a tanker travelling in a restricted and unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz was damaged and caught fire after hitting a naval mine, preventing it from moving," the statement said. Iranian naval authorities also warned vessels against attempting uncoordinated passage through the waterway, stating, "The Strait of Hormuz is closed to violating ships that intend to pass through prohibited and unsafe areas without coordination and relying on the lies of the US President."Senior Iranian military officials have also reiterated that the waterway would remain closed until Tehran's conditions were met. "The Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's conditions are met, under the control of the warriors of Islam," Major General Yazidi said, according to IRIB. The developments come as Washington weighs its military and diplomatic options regarding Iran. The Wall Street Journal reported that the head of the US military's Central Command, Admiral Brad Cooper, briefed US President Donald Trump on military options for Iran during a White House meeting on Thursday. The meeting was also attended by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman General Dan Caine and other Cabinet members, the newspaper reported, citing US officials and people familiar with the discussions. The deliberations come amid reports of a possible resumption of major US combat operations against Iran, following the US-Israeli bombing campaign earlier this year on February 28. Washington has also increased air defences, munitions and other supplies across the Middle East in recent weeks, according to the report. (ANI)
